one_liner: Single-header C++11 command-line parser in the style of Python argparse; its 2016 benchmark ran 2.2x faster than Boost.Program_options.
what_it_does: Parses argv into statically typed argument objects: you build an args::ArgumentParser, register Flag, ValueFlag<T>, ValueFlagList<T>, CounterFlag, MapFlag, Positional<T> and PositionalList<T> objects on it, call ParseCLI(argc, argv) or ParseArgs(vector), then read values with args::get(). It also generates wrapped help text, nests validation groups (Xor, AtLeastOne, AllOrNone, custom predicates), supports git-style subcommands, nargs flags, custom readers and bash completion. It is not a drop-in for Boost.Program_options: there is no options_description/variables_map and no config-file source; each option is a typed C++ object.
how_it_is_fast: No named algorithm: the speed comes from a light object model rather than a clever parser. Each argument object stores its typed value directly, the parser walks the argument vector once and assigns positionals as it goes (the README cites this choice 'for better simplicity and speed'), and flag lookup asks each child's Matcher, which holds the short and long names in an unordered_set<char> and an unordered_set<string>. Integers are converted with strtoll/strtoull and other types with an istringstream pinned to the classic locale.
when_to_use: A C++11 CLI tool that wants argparse-style features (typed flags, lists, maps, counters, help text, bash completion) from one dependency-free header.
Programs with non-trivial option logic: nested validation groups (Xor, AtLeastOne, AllOrNone, user predicates) or git-like subcommands with shared arguments.

Code that parses many command lines in-process (test harnesses, REPL or chat-command front ends reusing CLI syntax), where about 9 microseconds per build-and-parse (2016 figure) beats Boost.Program_options and TCLAP.
Projects that cannot take Boost or a compiled library: copy args.hxx, or install via CMake, meson, conan, buck or tipi.
when_not_to_use: Choosing on speed alone: a CLI parses once per process, the gap is microseconds, and the published numbers are from args 2.0.0 (May 2016), not the current 6.6.0.
You need config-file or environment-variable sources merged with the command line, as Boost.Program_options offers; args parses argument vectors only.
Order-sensitive flags (like GNU find), mixed prefix styles in one parser, or a positional list before other positionals: the README says the library will never support these.
Non-ASCII flag names or help text with combining characters: UTF-8 support is limited and unnormalized, and Windows-style '/' short prefixes have had an open bug (#26) since 2017.
You want new features or friendly group-validation messages: the author calls it feature-complete, and failed group validation only reports that the whole expression failed.

integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (meson default cpp_std=c++11); CMake 3.10 for the package; old MSVC (_MSC_VER <= 1800) gets a noexcept shim
integration.platforms: any; CI builds and tests on ubuntu-latest, macos-latest and windows-latest in Debug and Release, plus a meson job on Ubuntu
integration.thread_safety: not documented; parser and argument objects hold mutable parse state, so give each thread its own parser

gotchas: Benchmark provenance: the README's run output (0.895472 s args, 1.45001 s TCLAP, 1.98972 s Boost) is byte-identical in the README at tag 2.0.0 (May 2016), where the benchmark used the pre-4.0.0 API (ArgFlag, ArgFlagList, PosArgList, integer.value). The source was later rewritten to ValueFlag/PositionalList but never re-run, so the numbers measure args 2.0.0 and a 2016-era TCLAP and Boost. Today's constructors run duplicate-flag detection over the whole parser tree on every flag added, rebuilding two hash sets each time, which makes construction quadratic in flag count, and that construction is inside the timed loop; current speed is unmeasured.

Errors and control flow use exceptions: --help arrives as a thrown args::Help, completion as args::Completion, bad input as ParseError, ValidationError or RequiredError, and a duplicate flag name throws ParseError from the flag's constructor, outside the try block around ParseCLI in the README examples. Define ARGS_NOEXCEPT to get error codes through GetError() instead.
Integer values go through strtoll/strtoull with base 0, kept on purpose in PRs #164 and #177: '0x10' parses as 16, '010' as 8, and '08' is rejected.
A ValueFlag given twice silently keeps the last value unless it was built with Options::Single (then ExtraError), and the first PositionalList swallows every positional after it.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The catalogued siblings (lexy, re2c, winnow, chumsky, flap, the pika parser) parse text against grammars, and none of them parses argv. Pick args when the input is a command line, and one of those when you are parsing a language or file format.
verified_claims_summary: The author's micro-benchmark (g++ -O2 -std=c++11; compiler, Boost and TCLAP versions and CPU not stated) builds a parser and parses the 13-token line '-i 7 -c a 2.7 --char b 8.4 -c c 8.8 --char d' 100,000 times with asserts enabled: args 0.895 s, TCLAP 1.450 s, Boost.Program_options 1.990 s, so Boost takes 2.22x and TCLAP 1.62x as long (about 9 microseconds per iteration for args). The run dates from args 2.0.0 in May 2016, and the Boost loop skips po::notify.
status_note: Feature-complete but still patched: 6.6.0 was tagged 2026-07-22, the last commit is 2026-10-05, and many 2026 hardening PRs went in; MIT, a single header with CI on Linux, macOS and Windows, safe to vendor.
